modes.note: "starting at $1/Hour". Login time summed per day and rounded up to the next whole hour. Physical non-VM Mac, but a managed user account without admin/root: not a sandbox. Engine encoding: per-minute with no per-login minimum; the real bill rounds each DAY's summed login time up to the next hour (adds < 1 h per Mac per day).

plans.name: Self-serve
plans.note: Group/Team and customised solutions by quote. RAM, storage, network, 4K/eGPU add-ons priced at checkout (not captured).

free.conditions: No Dedicated or PAYG trial. First-time Managed subscription offers 24 hours; checkout also contains a hidden Runner/Agent plan with a 48-hour trial.

caveats: Dedicated prices from the live Dedicated page ($59 Intel / $89 M1 / $114 M2 / $164 M4 per month). The checkout plan picker says "Dedicated Server starting at US$49/month" (config/cycle not shown). providers/macincloud.json had M4 $124.99 and M2 $99 from third-party comparison pages; superseded.
"Dedicated" is a dedicated macOS instance ("Instance on Physical Mac Server"), i.e. a VM with 4 cores by default, not a whole Mac.

PAYG and Managed plans are non-admin user accounts on shared Macs (flagged alt): no root, no provisioning API; suited to humans, not agents. PAYG page text says both "prepay 30 hours" and "prepaid 25-Hour" credit.
PAYG hourly/daily spec (vCPU/RAM) depends on the chosen Mac; vcpu/ram left null so the engine will not size-match them.
Bandwidth: "100/1000 Mbps Port Speed"; no egress price published (null). Static IP included.
No macOS VM-per-Mac cap disclosure; Apple macOS SLA: leasing a Mac requires a minimum lease of 24 consecutive hours with sole use by the lessee, and allows at most 2 additional macOS VMs per Mac.
Shared Mac, no admin: Pay-as-You-Go and Managed plans are non-admin user accounts on a shared physical Mac (checkout.macincloud.com: "No Admin/Root Access").

Managed Server starting prices are hour-limited variants. Live checkout shows 3-hour and 8-hour daily-limit variants; support confirms usage above an Hour Daily Limit is $1 per extra hour and can trigger automatic adjustment to a larger daily limit. Exact total varies by platform/RAM/term and is not modelled.
Intel Dedicated ($59/mo, macOS Sonoma only) is still on sale but encoded as legacy so the Apple-silicon M1 ($89/mo) is the priced option.

Checkout contains but hides a $29/month Runner/Agent plan (Azure Pipelines, GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab and TeamCity; no remote desktop; 48-hour trial). It is announced in checkout data but not currently selectable, so it is not an estimator mode.
Dedicated checkout contains a Docker Dev preset and Jenkins flavor but both are disabled. Do not infer Docker-inside or an available Linux/Docker plan from these announced controls.

Checkout exposes 10 routing/location choices: LA, Dallas, New York, South America from US East, London, Frankfurt, Mumbai, Singapore, Perth and Sydney. Coarse card regions remain correctly US/EU/Asia/other; the South America choice is routed from US East.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

extras.price: +$5/month each on the base managed configuration

snapshot_auto.quote: We highly recommend that you backup your critical files before attempting to upgrade your Dedicated server's OS.
snapshot_auto.note: Servers are monthly/weekly subscriptions that run continuously (no stop/sleep/idle lifecycle to snapshot); the portal only offers Reboot. No snapshot or automatic backup feature anywhere in plan pages, checkout options or KB (KB search for 'snapshot' returns nothing); users are told to back up their own files.

snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/image/clone action in the web portal or checkout configurator (options: OS, platform, CPU, RAM, internal/external disk, RDP, bandwidth, SSH; disabled Firewall/VPN/GPU). Changing macOS on Managed plans means buying a new subscription. No API.

harness_api.quote: You will receive a static IP address and Virtual Network Computing (VNC) access for connecting to the server, after which you will have full control over the server to set up other connection methods if you prefer (such as with TeamViewer, NoMachine, or other software).
harness_api.note: Human remote-desktop product with no provisioning or control API at all, let alone an agent-harness API. Only non-interactive product is the Azure/VSTS build-agent plan.

guest_firewall.note: Dedicated plan = macOS instance (VM on a physical Mac) with 'Full macOS administrator/root/sudo access', so the macOS pf packet filter (not nftables/iptables) can be configured. Not possible on Managed/Pay-As-You-Go (non-admin user accounts on a shared physical Mac).

secret_proxy.quote: Files must be sent to and from the Mac server using cloud storage services or email attachments.
secret_proxy.note: No secrets or credential feature of any kind; credentials live on the Mac itself (keychain/files).

volume_attach.quote: If you upgraded your Dedicated server with an external hard drive you will need to format it before use with the following steps:
volume_attach.note: Dedicated only: 'External Hard Drive' add-on, 50-500 GB at $10 per 50 GB per month, upgradable later (not downgradable). The live checkout config disables it for Apple-silicon platforms (M1/M2/M4) and for Sequoia/Ventura/Monterey/Big Sur, so in practice it is the legacy Intel option; Apple-silicon plans get bigger internal disks instead (250 GB included, +$10 per 50 GB).

volume_shared.quote: We highly recommend using a cloud storage service such as Google Drive or DropBox.
volume_shared.note: The external drive is attached to one server; no shared/network filesystem product. File sharing between servers is via third-party sync (Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, Box).
